EW/FW: fund weighting within a vintage (equal, or by fund size). $q_v$: vintage weights, $w_v=Vq_v/\sum_uq_u$; $q_v=1$ is the main specification, $q_v=n_v$ (the vintage's fund count) a robustness check. SE$_A$: Bartlett (Newey--West) sandwich over vintage years with truncation $S=\lceil 1.3\sqrt{V}\rceil$; markers from two-sided Kiefer--Vogelsang fixed-$b$ $p$-values at $b=S/V$: $^{*}$\,$p<0.05$, $^{**}$\,$p<0.01$, $^{***}$\,$p<0.001$. For $q_v=n_v$ only point estimates are reported: in a Monte Carlo on data shaped like ours the sandwich SE of these estimates is 0.49--0.61 of their sampling standard deviation and the test rejects a true $\beta_{MKT}$ in 12--20\% of samples at the 5\% level (3.3--6.4\% for $q_v=1$). $^{\dagger}$\,estimate on a bound of the admissible domain ($\beta_{MKT}\in[-1,4]$, $\alpha\in[-2\%,2\%]$ per month, monthly gross benchmark return $1+r_f+\theta^\top F_t\ge 0.08$ over the estimation window); SE$_A$ and marker not reported. Full-sample fits only (no cross-validation or jackknife for this criterion). $S=7$, $V=23$, $b=0.304$.}
